narr: A second winter storm impacted Southwestern California. The heaviest rainfall impacted San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties where rainfall totals ranged from 2 to 4 inches across the coast with 5 to 10 inches across the foothills and mountains. For Ventura and Los Angeles counties, rainfall totals ranged between 0.50 and 1.50 inches with local amounts up to 3 inches across the foothills. The heavy rainfall produced numerous reports of flooding across San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties. Also, gusty south to southwest winds were reported across many areas.
ev: Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding near the community of Atascadero in San Luis Obispo county. California Highway Patrol reported mud and rocks across Highway 41.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding in Santa Barbara county. Highway 135 was closed from Bell Street to the Harris Grade, due to significant mud and water flowing across the roadway.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding in San Luis Obispo county. California Highway Patrol reported road closures between Avila Beach Drive and San Luis Bay drive, due to flooding.
California Highway Patrol reported Chimney Rock Road was completely washed out, due to heavy rain and flash flooding.
California Highway Patrol reported significant flooding in the community of Cambria in San Luis Obispo county. At a gas station, water rose to a depth up to half of the gas pumps.
California Highway Patrol reported mud and debris completely blocking York Mountain Road and Shadow Canyon Road.
California Highway Patrol reported mud and debris blocking the offramp of Highway 154.
